rows.prediction:
The problem shown in the image is known as the "Pythagorean Triangle" or the "Pythagorean Problem." It is a classic problem in Euclidean geometry that dates back to ancient Greece, specifically to the Pythagorean Brotherhood, a group of philosophers and mathematicians who were active in the 6th century BCE.

The problem is as follows: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the length of the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of the other two sides. This is known as the Pythagorean theorem.

The history of the Pythagorean theorem is intertwined with the history of mathematics and the development of Euclidean geometry. The theorem was first formulated by the Pythagoreans, who were known for their interest in the relationships between numbers and the physical world. The theorem was later formalized by the Greek mathematician Euclid in his "Elements," which is a foundational text in the field of mathematics.

The Pythagorean theorem has had a significant impact on mathematics and science, and it continues to be a fundamental concept in geometry and trigonometry. It has been used in various applications, including surveying, navigation, and computer graphics.
